Methods and statistical benchmark

Cariaco Lab Data Explorer · Version 1.2.0 · Updated 20 September 2026

Intended for exploratory use. The application helps visualize, screen, and summarize data. It does not replace a prespecified analysis plan or review in specialist statistical software.

What was checked

The browser calculations were tested on 18 deterministic stress datasets and compared with R 4.6.1 using base R, car 3.1-5, nlme 3.1-169, and rstatix 1.1.0. D'Agostino–Pearson results were compared with SciPy 1.13.1. All 1,044 numerical comparisons passed their declared tolerances, and eight invalid or degenerate edge cases were rejected as intended.

MethodsStatusMain limitation
Descriptive statistics, t-tests, classical and Welch one-way ANOVA, correlations and linear regressionMatched RStudy-design and model assumptions still apply.
Mann–Whitney, Wilcoxon, Kruskal–Wallis, Friedman and Dunn post-testsMatched RAsymptotic calculations with documented tie and continuity corrections.
Holm, Bonferroni, Šidák and Benjamini–Hochberg correctionsMatched R/formulaCorrection family must reflect the analysis plan.
Two-way Type III ANOVA with sum contrastsMatched R fixturesRequires estimable effects and appropriate residual assumptions.
Random-intercept modelMatched R stress fixturesOne random intercept only; denominator df remain approximate. Confirm mixed models externally.
Shapiro–WilkSame decisions; small numerical differencesAll α = 0.05 decisions matched R, but confirm results close to the threshold.
D'Agostino–Pearson K²Matched SciPyUsed as a secondary diagnostic when n ≥ 20.
Four-parameter logistic fitExploratory onlyParameter confidence intervals are not implemented; confirm final estimates externally.

Assumptions to review

  • Rows missing a selected variable are excluded from that analysis.
  • Tests are two-sided unless explicitly stated otherwise; diagnostic labels use α = 0.05.
  • Normality tests use model residuals; paired analyses use within-subject differences. A non-significant result does not prove normality.
  • Outlier procedures flag observations but never remove them automatically.
  • Automatic suggestions cannot identify pseudoreplication, confounding, or the true experimental unit.
  • Repeated two-factor data are blocked from ordinary two-way ANOVA and require a suitable mixed or repeated-measures model.
  • Pairwise post-tests are simple comparisons, not estimated-marginal-means contrasts.
  • Volcano plots visualize user-supplied effects and p/FDR values; they do not fit an omics model.

How the application was made

It is a static React and TypeScript application built with Vite. Data and calculations remain in the visitor's browser; no ChatGPT, OpenAI API, database, or application server is required. Charts are rendered in the browser, while the two normality routines are supplied by a WebAssembly statistics library.
